cohort: The study included 12,567 women with a mean age of 49.9 years, participating in a large population-based health survey in Norway.
finding: Age, educational level, diarrhea, constipation, birthweight, and obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASIS) increased the risk of anal incontinence in all women.
mod_finding: Women with vaginal deliveries complicated by OASIS are at increased risk of anal incontinence, but no increased risk was found in nulliparous women, women who had cesarean sections only, or women with vaginal deliveries not complicated by OASIS.
